title: Engine Sound
author: Harlan_42
selftext:
Working on a racing simulation game and the racing needs engine noise.  It never occurred to me that this was a tough thing to implement.  Then Claude put in his version that sounds technical and sterile.  Claude suggested a few articles, and my take was you want to run multiple channels to create the sound.    
The problem is the transition of the loop recordings.  I staggered the channels so that the transition was a lot less noticeable.  Claude added code to tie the play speed to the car speed.  And we use volume based on number of cars around.  
What I get is more like an engine drone with subtle changes.  Turned on the sites background music to take the focus off the engine.  
My latest thought is to add one channel that doesn't loop but is the length of a full acceleration.  The source comes from clipping 8 secs from a longer clip taking the longes acceleration.  I hope to run it while the car is speeding up.  I can shorten the play time and repeat so it sounds like a car shifting gears.    
I am going to have Claude implement it as soon as he gets back into town tomorrow.    
Anybody have any other ideas about implementing racing engine sounds?

comments.author: Navadvisor
comments.body: That's pretty cool, you could find some assets for relatively cheap too.

comments.author: xavium
comments.body:
You want to tie it to RPM (and ideally throttle) rather than just pure speed. And have a sample for each step of the way (say every 500rpm or so), so they're not too stretched. Then crossfade between them based on the rpm from the game. 

That way when you throttle, you can have variability depending on how much it increases (or decreases when letting off the throttle) the rpm of the engine, not just purely the speed of the vehicle. 

If you wanted to, go further by layering it with exhaust, engine, intake and turbo etc. if you're in the interior they'll sound different to exterior. 

Hope this helps!!

comments.author: schuettla
comments.body:
I also work with claude (opus 5.5) and for me it was the model that just came up with a webaudio simulation of a v8 motor. And it sounds fine. You can listen to it here: [https://holzbauer.info/dev/monstertruck/](https://holzbauer.info/dev/monstertruck/)

I have also made another racing game, where I just gave the model the idle and acceleration car sound as mp3 and the model was able to modulate, pitch it etc. so that it sounded accurate when accelerating.

So in my opinion, just prompt is what you want but make sure u use a top tier model
